source.title: Hierarchical Latent Structures in Data Generation Process Unify Mechanistic Phenomena across Scale
source.authors: Jonas Rohweder; Subhabrata Dutta; Iryna Gurevych

page_placements.theme: Self-repair after ablation is common but partial, and its size varies with model, data and training

record.tranche_reason: The study measures Hydra-effect compensation using layer- and head-ablation, but does not test the named copy-suppression head or any of the specific claim versions. Its measurements bear on the broader self-repair behavior in a different data setting.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses copy suppression as a prior proposed account of the Hydra effect and cites the original study, but does not analyze L10H7, copy suppression, its QK/OV circuits, calibration, or the 76.9% loss figure. Rows cover only the paper's own Hydra-effect ablation results. Induction, function-vector, gradient-similarity, curvature, and syntax-probe results do not measure the claim's behavior and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study mentions copy suppression only in its introduction and related work, as a prior partial account of the Hydra effect. Its own results are generic Hydra-effect compensation scores from layer and head ablation in toy, PCSG, N-gram and OLMo-1B models. It never identifies copy-suppression heads, measures suppression of predicted-and-copied tokens, or splits self-repair by mechanism. None of V1–V6 is tested. The reader's 'tests'/T2 is wrong. Generic self-repair measured without isolating copy suppression is a related but different construct, so it goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that hierarchical latent structure in the data-generation process is a major driver of induction heads, function vectors and the Hydra effect. This holds jointly with decorrelated gradients and directional concavity, which they find necessary but not sufficient. They draw no new conclusion about L10H7 or copy suppression.
record.recipe_differences: The original analyzes GPT-2 small L10H7 and its copy-suppression circuits and loss effect. This study instead uses layer- and head-ablation to measure general Hydra compensation in toy and synthetic-data models, and layer ablation in PCSG, N-gram, and OLMo models.
record.method_sensitivity: Hydra results differ with data-generation condition (hierarchical versus flat); layerwise ablation produces a weaker signal than headwise ablation in the toy experiment. In the comparative experiment, compensation is reported to localize in middle layers after training.

fits_no_version.finding: Headwise Hydra compensation is much higher in a toy model trained on hierarchical data than on flat data (d=1.82, p<0.001). The layerwise signal is weaker and does not survive Bonferroni correction. PCSG-trained and OLMo-1B models show layerwise compensation; the N-gram model shows none.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hierarchical latent structure in training data promotes generic Hydra-effect self-repair; flat N-gram data does not.

record.problems: The toy experiment uses 10 matched seed pairs. Layerwise Hydra significance does not survive Bonferroni correction. The large-model Hydra outcomes are described qualitatively and shown in a figure without tabulated values; the PCSG and N-gram comparison uses custom 17M models, while OLMo-1B is a reference model rather than a matched training condition.
record.rows_left_out: No other Hydra rows left out. Induction-head, function-vector, gradient-decorrelation, curvature, and parse-tree results were omitted because they do not measure the claim's behavior.

untested.parts: No analysis of GPT-2 small, L10H7, or suppression of predicted tokens that also appear in context.
No QK/OV circuit analysis and no loss attribution (the 76.9% figure).
Measures overall downstream compensation after ablation. Does not ablate an upstream copier or show that reduced suppression drives the compensation.
No identification of negative or copy-suppression heads in other tasks or models.
Does not estimate copy suppression's share of self-repair, or compare it with LayerNorm rescaling or other mechanisms.

record.verdict_notes: Copy suppression appears only as background (McDougall et al. 2023, cited as a partial account of the Hydra effect). The Hydra metric is the change in the downstream layer's logit projection after ablation; it does not decompose compensation by mechanism. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No analysis of GPT-2 small L10H7, token copying, context occurrences, or ordinary-text behavior.
No QK or OV circuit analysis, loss attribution, or 76.9% result.
Measures generic Hydra-effect compensation, but does not ablate an upstream copier or test whether reduced copied evidence explains compensation.
No test of whether negative heads in other tasks, models, or sizes share the copy-suppression role; cited examples are background only.
Does not compare copy suppression with other mechanisms or estimate copy suppression's share of self-repair.

rows.subject: Transformer (toy model)
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed individual attention-head value outputs and measured maximum downstream predictive-influence compensation.
rows.measure: Peak headwise Hydra score; the paper reports consistently and substantially higher values than for the flat DGP, with large effect sizes across training summaries.
rows.value: Hierarchical DGP: consistently and substantially higher than flat DGP.
rows.uncertainty: For final, peak, and AUC summaries, paired t-tests and Wilcoxon tests reject the null at p < 0.001; headwise Hydra final effect size d = 1.82.
rows.locator: Section 4.3; Figure 1; Appendix B.2 and Figure 5
rows.note: Toy setup has 10 independent matched seed pairs. The text reports the comparison and tests, but not the underlying score values.

rows.subject: Transformer (toy model)
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed an upstream layer's residual contribution and measured downstream predictive-influence change.
rows.measure: Peak layerwise Hydra score; reported as weaker than the headwise signal.
rows.value: Hierarchical DGP: weaker positive signal than for headwise ablation.
rows.uncertainty: One-sided significance p < 0.05 did not survive Bonferroni correction.

rows.note: The authors attribute the weaker result to coarse layer ablation, which removes multiple heads whose effects may partially cancel.

rows.subject: PCSG-trained model

rows.measure: Layerwise Hydra-effect compensation across checkpoints; described as substantial and higher than OLMo-1B.
rows.baseline: OLMo-1B reference is reported as showing compensation, at a lower degree.
rows.value: Substantial compensation; higher degree than OLMo-1B.
rows.note: The plotted trajectory is not numerically tabulated in the text.
rows.check: The baseline is OLMo-1B, a different, unmatched model used as a reference, not a control. The matched control is the N-gram model (r6). The text gives no numbers, only a figure.
